newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson profits up on strong mobile phone sales.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson profits up on strong mobile phone sales.

text.p: AB LM Ericsson, the Swedish telecommunications giant, reported surprisingly good first-half results Thursday, boosted by a sharp advance in sales of mobile phones.
The company said pre-tax profit soared 44 percent to 6.1 billion crowns ($781 million) in the first half, about 16 percent higher than the market consensus.
A weaker Swedish crown boosted the result by about 500 million crowns ($64 million), the company said.
Besides healthy growth figures for revenues and orders, which rose 44 percent and 39 percent, respectively, Ericsson said, mobile telephone sales more than doubled in the period.
Net sales for the group amounted to 72.2 billion crowns ($9.2 billion) in the period, with mobile telephone sales doubling to 18.39 billion crowns ($2.36 billion) from 9.09 billion ($1.16 billion).
Ericsson's result puts it in a league with Motorola Inc., whose better-than-expected profits for the second quarter earlier this month pushed its shares to a two-year high.

Ericsson announced separately that it signed a 1.55 billion crown ($200 million) equipment supply deal with BellSouth Corp. to supply its customers with technology that provides mobile phone users with functions like caller identification, security services and short messaging systems.
